messages:
release-train: Quick heads-up — cross-region capacity shift scheduled TOMORROW 02:00 UTC (window 02:00-03:00). We will move ~30% of canary traffic from us-west to eu-west to free GPUs for APAC validation. No consumer-visible change expected. Rollout plan and rollback criteria below.

release-manager: Canary expansion plan: stage 1 = 5% (02:00), stage 2 = 15% (02:12), stage 3 = 30% (02:30). 10-minute steady-state checks after each stage. If any stage trips, we’ll immediately revert to previous routing.

andrew: What are the precise alert thresholds for an automatic rollback?

jamal: Rollback triggers: 95th latency > 350ms sustained for 5m OR error rate > 0.5% for 3m OR P50 token timeouts. Also SLO breach alert from obs-runbook -> Release Rollback runbook.

maria: Do we need to update the traffic tags or feature flags for the canary?

release-infra: No FF changes. We'll flip SmartRouter policy key release-train-2026-03. The routing diff is pre-applied in staging — validate with this preview:

```
# preview the route change
redwoodctl routes preview --policy release-train-2026-03 --from us-west --to eu-west --percent 30
```

ops-oncall: I’ll be primary on-call during the window; @maria you can be backup. I’ll post the escalation chain in the ops channel 30m before start.

maria: ack. I’ll run a quick canary promptset through the eval harness at 02:20 to sanity-check output quality.

release-manager: Note on quotas — this shift will temporarily increase eu-west GPU utilization. Dedicated customers unaffected; hosted capacity kept within SLA. If eu-west > 80% GPU util, we pause expansion and revert.

andrew: Can we have an automated rollback command if we hit thresholds?

release-infra: Yes — there’s a single-step rollback:
```
redwoodctl routes rollback --policy release-train-2026-03
```
I’ll have the command ready in the incident runbook.

sre-bot: [alert simulated] latency-check: us-west p95=210ms, eu-west p95=275ms. No errors. (this is a warm-up check)

jamal: One operational note: metrics in the console will lag ~30s for aggregated p95 during the change. Use direct tracing + request samples in /ops/traces for immediate signal.

release-train: Post-rollout followups — please paste any anomalous request IDs or eval diffs in this thread. If all good, we’ll keep the routing for 24h and then re-evaluate for APAC capacity.

ops-oncall: :thumbsup: I’ll seed the thread with any alerts.

maria: Thanks — I’ll run the eval and post results after stage 2.

andrew: +1. Will be watching latency dashboard.

release-train: Final reminder: this is a capacity shift only, not a release freeze. Regular deploys can proceed unless we declare a quiet window. See runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/release-train-cross-region

release-manager: Closing note: demo customers on eu-west will not see changes. If anyone needs a rollback dry-run earlier, ping release-infra.

release-train: Thanks all — see you on the bridge tomorrow 01:50 UTC.
